verdict.rationale: Stripe Identity's own docs say it generates events every time a verification session changes status, and the guide shows how to implement webhooks so the integration reacts to results automatically, without polling. That covers the core lifecycle-webhook capability. However, the pack never documents webhook signing or names the individual event types. missing for 10: evidence that webhooks are cryptographically signed with signature verification, explicit enumeration of the created/processing/verified/requires-input event types, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, verification lifecycle events arrive as signed webhooks — created, processing, verified, requires-input — so my system reacts to outcomes without polling

citations.quote: Stripe generates events every time a session changes status. In this guide, we’ll implement webhooks to notify your app when verification results become available.
Listen for verification results so your integration can automatically trigger reactions.
This API tracks a verification, from initial creation through the entire verification process, and shows verification results upon completion.
